column3: Close to the Aramaic.
“In the taste of the wine” is rendered “When Belshazzar tasted the wine.”
“They had brought out” is rendered with a passive, “had been taken out.”
Close to the Aramaic.
“At that moment” is rendered “Suddenly,” “candlestick” “lampstand,” and “palm of the hand” “back of the hand.”
“His brightness changed him” is rendered “the king’s face grew pale,” and “the joints of his loins were loosened” “his hip joints went slack.”
“With power” is rendered “aloud,” “astrologers” “diviners,” and “third in the kingdom he will rule” “have authority as third ruler.”
Close to the Aramaic.
“His brightness was changing” is rendered “his face grew even paler,” and “dumbfounded” “perplexed.”
“Before the words” is rendered “because of the words,” and “the house of the feast” “the banquet hall.”
“Astrologers” is rendered “diviners”; NASB keeps the repeated “your father.”
“Understanding” is rendered “knowledge,” “riddles” “enigmas,” and “loosening of knots” “solving of difficult problems.”
“You are Daniel” is rendered as a question, “Are you that Daniel … ?”; “sons of the exile” is rendered “exiles.”
Close to the Aramaic.
“Matter” is rendered “message”; NASB adds “Just.”
“Loosen knots” is rendered “solve difficult problems.”
“Another” is rendered “someone else”; NASB adds “or.”
“Kingdom” is rendered “sovereignty,” and “greatness” “grandeur.”
“Letting live” is rendered “spared alive,” “lifting up” “elevated,” and “bringing low” “humbled.”
“His spirit grew strong to act presumptuously” is rendered “his spirit became so proud that he behaved arrogantly”; “throne of his kingdom” is rendered “royal throne.”
“They made his heart with the animals” is rendered “his heart was made like that of beasts”; “they fed him” is rendered as a passive.
“Because” is rendered “even though.”
“Knowing” is rendered “understand,” and “breath” “life-breath.”
“Palm of the hand” is rendered “the hand.”
NASB transliterates the words as “MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN.”
“Finished it” is rendered “put an end to it.”
“Lacking” is rendered “deficient.”
“Broken in two” is rendered “divided.”
NASB supplies “put” and adds “now”; “having mastery” is rendered “had authority.”
“Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans” is rendered “Belshazzar the Chaldean king.”
